content.comment_body: I'm trying to update [product_name] from [version_no] to [version_no], but it isn't working. My computer runs Windows 7 32-bit since my hardware requires it. I downloaded the update for win32 and tried installing it both with and without a virtual machine, but I get an error as shown in the image. Is the installer supposed to work for 32-bit, or is there an issue? I also tried installing on another machine with Windows 7 64-bit (using the 64-bit installer), and that worked. Java and Visual C++ 2015 are both up to date. Could you check if the installer is correct? I've always used this Windows 7 32-bit machine for programming with [product_name], and updates have always worked before. Thanks for your help.
Please consider submitting a support request.

[product_name] [version_no] requires at least Windows 7 64-bit, according to the manual and sales information: 'Windows: Windows 7 (64 bit), Windows 8 (64 bit), Windows 10 (32/64 bit), or Windows 11. Linux: SUSE Linux 15 (64 bit). Mac OS: 10.14 Mojave, 10.15 Catalina, 11 Big Sur, 12.1 Monterey. Recommended Java Runtime Environment: Amazon Corretto 11.0.13.8.1.'

[product_name] [version_no] can technically be installed on Windows 7 32-bit, as the necessary files are available. However, you need the most up-to-date version of Windows 7 32-bit, and the software will run even slower than usual on this setup.

I've already tried installing from this folder with and without a virtual machine. It still doesn't work, showing the same error mentioned earlier. I was able to install the software on a different machine running Windows 10, which resolved my issue for now. It seems the Java VM included with the installer isn’t functional for 32-bit systems (that's my guess).
Please consider opening a support request.

analysis.insight_summary: Users trying to update [product_name] from [version_no] to [version_no] on Windows 7 32-bit face installation issues. While documentation specifies support only for 64-bit Windows, some users claim installation on 32-bit is possible but leads to very poor performance. There is confusion about compatibility, discrepancies in documentation, and frustration over lack of support for legacy systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to install and work on Windows 7 32-bit like previous versions, and hope that new installers maintain compatibility with older hardware and systems.
